<reason>B more convincingly isolates licensing’s marginal benefit: independent clearance before contested safety evidence becomes potentially irreversible public exposure. It directly answers pressure about upgrades, regulator expertise, and continuing access to authorized models. A raises legitimate delay, discretion, and competition costs, but repeatedly substitutes absolute claims of ineffectiveness for comparison with B’s bounded proposal. B’s administrative safeguards do not establish frictionless implementation, leaving A a meaningful objection, but B better explains why its preventive benefit justifies the additional burden.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s foreign-availability challenge materially damages A’s case: overseas access also limits withdrawal powers, and neither policy needs perfect containment to reduce EU exposure. A distinguishes targeted withdrawal from general preclearance but never adequately answers why licensing cannot reduce ordinary EU exposure.</best_rebuttal>
